reference: Kinoshita, A., Jose, F.A., Sundaram, D., Paixão, J.S., Soares, I.R.M., Figueiredo, A.M., Baffa, O. (2011) Electron spin resonance dating of teeth from Western Brazilian megafauna - preliminary results. Radiation Measurements 46, 842-846. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.radmeas.2011.05.004
software_detail: ROSY for all published ages; DATA (Grün 2009) also run and said to give the same results (no DATA ages printed)

conventions.cosmic: 114 uGy/a (printed 'mGy/y'), Prescott & Hutton (1994) from latitude, longitude and altitude
conventions.gamma_source: computed from mean of three soil samples (NAA)

sediment.note: average and standard deviation of the three soil samples (study-level 'soil_samples') were used, per Table 1 footnote; average not printed

samples.provenance: Table 1 (p. 844, NAA), Table 2 (p. 844, ROSY dose rates), Table 3 (p. 843, De and ages), sample 354
samples.notes: Dose rates printed 'mGy/a' but are uGy/a. External sediment dose rate (1127.37) excludes cosmic: 354 CU (1127.37+15.14+1771.32+114) = 3028 uGy/a -> 1300/3.028 = 429 ka (published 430). CU = EU dentine + LU enamel. Haplomastodon (Notiomastodon) teeth.

completeness: partial: no enamel/dentine thicknesses (only ~500 um etched off), no water content, no measured 234U/238U; ROSY dose-rate components per model are published
extraction_notes: Site 35 km north of Alta Floresta, Mato Grosso, Brazil. Tables read twice (separate prompts) with identical numbers. Note table numbering: Table 3 holds De and ages, Table 2 dose rates. K given in ppm in the paper.
